title: Agentic Email Conversations With Leads From a Mailbox You Own
summary: How to let an agent answer the leads who reply to you, on the same thread, from a mailbox your Cargo workspace owns: what it deploys, what the mailbox costs each month, the 5 to 40 sends a day warm-up ramp, and the suppression rules the send path enforces. A conversation agent, not a sequencer.
body_markdown:
**To let an agent hold email conversations with leads, give it one mailbox your workspace owns, lock every send to that mailbox, and wake the same chat when the lead replies or unsubscribes, plus once a day to check a quiet thread: it answers on the thread, sends at most one follow-up to silence, and stops on a no.** The[agentic engagement cookbook](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/agentic-engagement) declares that for a go-to-market team on Cargo: a sending domain, a mailbox, and one agent with a native email trigger and a heartbeat.


Be clear about what this is. It is the loop after a first email, for leads who are already in a conversation with you. It is not a sequencer, it does not blast a list, and it will not send a second unanswered email. If you need cadences across a list, keep the sequencer you have; Cargo connects to it.


## How it works, end to end#


1. **A domain and a mailbox.**` defineDomain` adopts a sending domain the workspace already bought in the Cargo app (` adopt: true` ).` defineMailbox` creates the From inbox on it, under a real person’s name. Domain, username and type are create-only: changing one destroys the inbox and starts a new one at the bottom of the ramp.
2. **The first send is yours.** A person asks the agent to start a thread in a chat, or a play calls the agent with a lead. The agent sends with the native` sendEmail` action, whose` mailboxUuid` is locked in the action config, so every send comes from that inbox.
3. **Replies wake the same chat.** A native email trigger with` kinds: \["replied", "unsubscribed"\]` starts a new turn in the chat that sent the email. Opens and clicks are left out on purpose: a tracking pixel is not a reason to write. Inbound mail from someone the agent never emailed does not open a chat.
4. **Silence gets one status check a day.** A heartbeat (` intervalMinutes: 1440` , at most 16 messages per chat) re-wakes a thread still at` sent` . The agent calls` listEmailEvents` to read the thread’s real status, sends at most one follow-up, and after that the conversation is over.
5. **Each wake sends at most once.** Before writing, the agent reads the workspace context so it only claims what you have written down, and checks status, basis, suppression and relevance. A reply carries` inReplyTo` and the full` references` chain, oldest first, so mail clients keep it in one thread. An unsubscribe, a bounce, “not interested” or a request for a human ends the loop.


## The mailbox: cost, ramp and the gates in the send path#


These are the numbers in Cargo’s code as of October 2026.


Item Value


Google mailbox 125 credits a month, for as long as it exists


Shared or private SMTP mailbox 100 credits a month


Each send (` sendEmail` ) 0.1 credits


Send ramp 5 a day at the start, rising linearly to 40 a day over 45 days of warm-up


Allowance window Rolling 24 hours, counting delivered mail only


A mailbox bills monthly until you remove it; there is no pause. Registering a new domain instead of adopting one is a separate, non-refundable charge. Read the live figures before you deploy:` cargo-ai mailboxManagement pricing get` .


The ramp only climbs once warm-up starts, which is a CLI call after deploy:` cargo-ai mailboxManagement mailbox start-warmup <uuid>` . A mailbox that never starts warm-up stays at 5 real sends a day.` mailbox get-send-allowance <uuid>` reports` dailyLimit` ,` sentCount` and` remainingCount` ; a send past the limit is refused with` dailyLimitReached` , not queued. The ramp is a ceiling, not a target.


What the send path enforces, in code:


- **Suppression is checked on every send.** Addresses are normalized, matched against the workspace-wide suppression list, and a match is refused as` recipientSuppressed` .
- **Every email carries a signed` List-Unsubscribe` link.** Using it writes a suppression row, so the next send to that address is refused. There is no command to remove a suppression.
- **An inactive mailbox does not send** (` mailboxNotActive` ).


What the code does not decide for you is your basis for writing to someone. The agent’s prompt requires one (they replied, they asked, a person asked it to start the thread), but a lawful basis and a relevant reason are yours to have before the first send.


## Run it#


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com        # emailed code, no browser, 100 free credits, no card


cargo-ai   project   cookbook   view   agentic-engagement
cargo-ai   project   add   cookbook/agentic-engagement      # from your Cargo project's root


```


Set the sending domain (` infra/domains/outreach.ts` ), the mailbox’s real first name, last name and username (` infra/mailboxes/rep.ts` ) and the agent’s` languageModel` . Then:


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   mailboxManagement   pricing   get          # say the monthly figure out loud before the next step
cargo-ai   project   plan                            # a "+ create mailbox" line is that monthly charge
cargo-ai   project   deploy
cargo-ai   mailboxManagement   mailbox   refresh-status   <  uui  d  >       # until "active"
cargo-ai   mailboxManagement   mailbox   start-warmup   <  uui  d  >


```


Then send one thread to yourself, reply to it, and check that the agent answers on the same thread without being prompted. Treat every send as live, which is why the first one goes to you.


## What it will not do#


- It does not send a list, run a cadence or send a second unanswered follow-up.
- It does not start a first send from a trigger or a heartbeat.
- It does not start warm-up, write to a CRM or manage DNS by default.
- It does not send from any mailbox but the one locked on the action, or to a suppressed address.
- It does not use Outlook mailboxes: that transport has not shipped.


The cookbook is marked **to-be-approved** : not yet deploy-verified against a live workspace. Treat its acceptance list as the test, starting with the test thread to yourself. If you would rather a person approves every reply,[answering positive replies with agents](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/answering-positive-replies-with-agents) describes that loop, and[AI SDR alternatives](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/ai-sdr-alternatives) compares the products that send for you.


## Frequently asked questions#


No. It answers leads who replied, on the same thread, and sends at most one follow-up to a thread that went quiet. A second unanswered email would be a sequence, and the agent is told to stop instead.


In Cargo’s code as of October 2026, a Google mailbox is 125 credits a month and a shared or private SMTP mailbox is 100, billed monthly until the mailbox is removed. Each send is 0.1 credits. Read the live figure with cargo-ai mailboxManagement pricing get before deploying.


Five a day until warm-up starts. Once it starts, the daily limit rises linearly to 40 over 45 days, measured over a rolling 24 hours. Stopping warm-up resets the ramp to five.


The unsubscribe link in every email writes a workspace-wide suppression, the trigger wakes the agent, and the agent does not send. Any later send to that address, from any mailbox in the workspace, is refused by the send path.
